ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jackie Robinson

code.originalText: Review after the retina consultation and first eye injections: retinal diagnosis, glucose, blood pressure and kidney medicines

text.paragraph: Review after the retina consultation and first eye injections: retinal diagnosis, glucose, blood pressure and kidney medicines. [S]

Mr. Robinson returns two days after his first visit, from the retina clinic this morning. Dr. Ostrowski-Lane examined both eyes with dilating drops, used ultrasound to confirm that the right retina is attached behind the blood, and measured the swelling at the center of each retina by OCT. She found proliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes with swelling of the macula in both, and bleeding into the gel of the right eye, and gave the first aflibercept injections in both eyes. His eyes are a little sore, as expected. He had no flashes or curtain over his vision. He asked how quickly his sugar should come down, because he wants it fixed at once, and what the injections will do. Chest tightness on stairs is unchanged; the stress test is booked. [S]

Laser to the right eye when the blood clears.

Same-day return for a curtain over the vision, flashes or a sudden loss.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). A1c 10.4%. A rapid fall in A1c can briefly worsen proliferative retinopathy, and semaglutide was linked to more retinopathy complications in a cardiovascular trial; the aim is a steady fall of about one point every three months, with the retina specialist watching monthly. [S]
Continue metformin and the slow glargine titration plan.
Empagliflozin 10 mg daily.
A GLP-1 receptor agonist to be considered once the retina specialist judges the retina stable.
Talking glucose meter and large-print plan.

Lisinopril increased to 40 mg.
Potassium and creatinine in four weeks.

Diabetic kidney disease with albuminuria (E11.22). eGFR 79 with a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 86 mg/g, raised also last year: G2 A2. An SGLT2 inhibitor and the highest ACE inhibitor dose protect kidneys and heart. [S]
Empagliflozin and lisinopril as above; written sick-day rules.

Follow-up: Stress test as booked. Second injections and review in four weeks with potassium and creatinine and the ankle-brachial index. Call for a curtain over the vision, flashes, eye pain with redness, chest pain at rest, dizziness, or vomiting (hold empagliflozin and lisinopril that day). Next scheduled visit 2026-08-26: four weeks after the new medicines: potassium and creatinine, blood pressure, ankle-brachial index, feet, mood, and the second eye injections. [S]
